# `silk/time/plain_year_month`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Months of specific years: the [`PlainYearMonth`](#PlainYearMonth) type, such as November 2026.

## When to use

Use [`PlainYearMonth`](#PlainYearMonth) for a value that names a whole month: the month of a bill, the expiry
of a card, a page of a calendar. For one day, use `PlainDate` of `silk.time.plain_date`.

## Details

Months are in the ISO 8601 calendar. The range is `-271821-04` to `+275760-09`, the months
in which `PlainDate` has dates. The text form is `YYYY-MM`.

## Examples

### Go through the months of a subscription

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }
import silk.time.plain_year_month { PlainYearMonth }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let start = PlainYearMonth.fromDate(PlainDate.make(2026, 11, 19))
  let end = start.addMonths(3)
  if end.year() != 2027 || end.month() != 2 || end.daysInMonth() != 28 {
    return 1
  }
  if start.monthsUntil(end) != 3 || !(&start < &end) {
    return 2
  }
  match end.atDay(28) {
    Option<PlainDate>.Some { value } => {
      if value.dayOfYear() != 59 {
        return 3
      }
    }
    Option<PlainDate>.None => {
      return 4
    }
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `PlainYearMonth` with `import silk.time.plain_year_month { PlainYearMonth }`.

## `PlainYearMonth`

```silk
pub struct PlainYearMonth
```

A month of one year, in the ISO 8601 calendar.

### Details

`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare in time order. `Display` writes `YYYY-MM`, with
a sign and six digits for a year outside 0 to 9999.

<a id="PlainYearMonth.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<PlainYearMonth, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a month from ISO 8601 text such as `2026-11`.

#### Details

The text is `YYYY-MM` or `YYYYMM`; a year outside 0 to 9999 has a sign and six digits.
Bracketed annotations can follow. The text can also be a whole date, with or without a
time, in the form that `PlainDate.parse` reads; the day is checked and then ignored.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the month is not from 1 to 12 or is outside the range.
- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.
